column8: Mon 16 Nov: conceit and 3d, what a founder's word rested on (future income, tied to others' money); drop the unsourced 'most famous'; quote the letter, never the archive's summary (row 7); 'endowment fund' is Rockefeller's word, never Laura's reserve.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d order (owned before she asks); say her ten operating payments, never ten years of operations (H9-119); the case gives no total, so never 'more than half done' or any share of a whole for Laura (SKELETON 3b; Q11e: first, never largest).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c store; a figure kept private until its frame was fixed, a tactical twin of the rule that no figure is stated before the move (NUMBERS 4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d context only; $549,000 against $400,000 (137%, Keel arithmetic) is one case and counts pledges; never a forecast for her co-sponsors; Q11a's field tests carry the general point.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a co-funder's condition on counting land; serves no part.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b hard top; her stated figure cannot rise, but IPS l.15 names a co-sponsor falling short as a use of the half kept, at her choice (CANON D12), so never say co-sponsors know she cannot cover them.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; CONFLICTING, S capped at 3; the letter governs (pledges by June 1890, payments from 90 days after), so quote Goodspeed's letter, never the archive's 90 days.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3a, Carnegie made running money a condition before bricks; say she owns her ten operating payments, a base not the whole budget (H9-119), never 'the running money'; drop 'asks co-sponsors only toward the building' (case p.3: operating support beyond her commitment may come from co-sponsors).

Mon 16 Nov: store; the parallel inverts (Carnegie made recipients carry running costs, Laura carries a base herself) and the endowed-institution clause argues against pre-funding; first quote only, if at all, never 'answers Carnegie's test'.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and Table 3 context; 225 offers lapsed for running budgets and for WWI building costs, with no count by reason, so it never shows running money alone; Lapham's author not read.

Mon 16 Nov: store; drop 'asks co-sponsors for nothing yearly, so this cannot happen to her': the case lets operating support beyond her commitment come from co-sponsors, and her $50,000 is a base (H9-119).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d and 3e; a stated grant cut after others planned on it ended a library; a 2024 blog with the Carnegie files not read, so S 3; her ends do not move after the move (NUMBERS 4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d, paid in advance ended the doubt when Perelman's fortune fell; the vivid counter-case to H7-070 (Lehman pledge) for why owned beats pledged; NYT read as the artdaily reprint.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b and 3e; the lead figure stayed fixed while the cost doubled and others filled the gap; never imply her flexibility (about $29,800 with the excess, NUMBERS 4) meets a doubling (aha 8 fix).
Mon 16 Nov: store; UNVERIFIED, S 2 at most: the LMDC condition read only on Wikipedia; read LMDC minutes or the grant agreement before any use.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, the nearest Chinese-speaking case found of a funder carrying a building figure plus running deficits; say her ten operating payments are owned, never 'running money' (H9-119); HKJC is a funder with yearly surpluses, not a founder.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b and 3e aha, a budget became a floor (HK$1.8bn to HK$3.8bn, 2.1 times, Keel arithmetic) while her top cannot follow it up (NUMBERS 4); a 2.1-times overrun is far beyond the half kept, so never 'the overrun is met from the half kept' (aha 8 fix).
Mon 16 Nov: 3b contrast; 'as necessary' with no top needs a yearly surplus; Laura's figure has a hard top (NUMBERS 4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3e context; Garden Bridge costs rose while pledges stalled; her stated ends are fixed after the move whatever the building costs (NUMBERS 4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d words; an auditor called anonymous pledges fragile; her figure is named and listed by identifier (Table 1's style); pairs with row 21.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d words; 'raised' covered pledges (£145m claimed against about £85m committed); 'owned' describes her money, while the written form funders count (SKELETON 3d, Q32) may still be a signed commitment; the £145m speaker not read.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; a public funder relied on verbal updates; co-sponsors can be shown her holdings by identifier and maturity.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 evidence beside the reserve ahas (Q9-016, Q51-035); the refused maintenance guarantee was the trigger, but a £70m capital gap stood at the same time (row 19), so never 'not the building'; say her ten operating payments are owned first, never 'her running money' (H9-119); never 'no other founder' (SKELETON 3.0).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d and 3e gap; co-sponsors will ask what happens to her money if the facility is cancelled, which NUMBERS and CANON do not answer; for the lead to decide or name as a 3e limit.
Mon 16 Nov: store; her owned figure removes the risk that her own figure fails, not a co-sponsor's risk that the project fails, so drop 'takes that risk off them'.

Mon 16 Nov: conceit only with care; Li's moved money stopped being his, while Laura's moved half stays hers in Treasuries (IPS l.15: money you already own) until the 2033 contribution, so never say it stops being hers; the parallel is money counted apart from the risky pool.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; use as a contrast, not a twin: Li's exit is open-ended (war or anything unforeseeable), the IPS names two (a missed deposit, a Treasury default).
Mon 16 Nov: store; one founder's phrase, not the floor word founders use; Q52 rows 31-33 show 'at least' sounds like ignorance from a speaker who knows, so the bottom is said as a plain figure.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d, claim 3's price of a cut figure (60% announced, 14.98% given); drop 'no regulator stands between her figure and the money': a fund's board can extend an end date (Table 3 row 4).
Mon 16 Nov: store; Chinese press tests stated gifts against what was paid; the row mixes two founders, so name each before use.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c store; a first phase stated in shares, later partly pledged as collateral; Q52-023 (Lilly) is the case where the share fell; never restate that she states only what she owns (aha 4's one home).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; the city's free land came with the 2021 signing beside the founder's 100億 (row 33), so never 'the founder paid first and the government followed'; 43% paid (Keel arithmetic).
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 32 (same university and agreement); 'neither conditional on the other' is inference, since the agreement itself was not read.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d client knowledge; UNVERIFIED, S 2 at most until 聯合報 13 Jul 2008 is read at the original; 曹興誠 was a donor, not a founder, and the sale was tied to quake relief from the start.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d Taiwan form, one exact sum in a contract with the city; one company's case, never 'Taiwan practice'; a contract would carry the bottom, the figure co-sponsors count (SKELETON 3d), with the top said as intended.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Broad capped the recipient's spending, not his own gift; a contrast only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d clause; an up-to match sat 58% untapped (Keel arithmetic); her top is owned and waits on no one.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3d store; Kroc paid half the running costs and made towns find the rest; Laura owns all ten operating payments, a base (H9-119); 'endowment' is Kroc's word, never her reserve's.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 evidence; Long Beach could neither build nor keep open and also had a site problem, so not running money alone; drop the claim that her hard top guards against donor creep (no evidence); the crowd-out is a 3b counterweight to Q11a.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q52-028 (Knight: a fixed sum, then more); raising a figure later is safe, as Arrow and Fisher's asymmetry in SKELETON 3b already says.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 14 (a lead figure fixed while the budget doubled); a Dutch museum, not Table 3's Taiwan building-cost trend.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; one case read (LACMA), so never 'the common form'; her figure first and unconditional on the money side (SKELETON 3d).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c aha, supports the rule: before the move the top hangs on a future event neither party controls (EWU), after it both ends are owned; EWU's own example, a pledge hanging on the donor's new clients, is IPS l.9's career point; a range counts at its bottom (Q71), so the bottom is the figure to count.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, co-sponsors build in reliance on her figure, the case for the binding written form; 'closely held stock' is unlisted shares, not VT, so never 'shares do not count until sold'; say counted gifts are specified and unconditional.
